# Wave 1C Tier-1 reflection card. Authored by sc:sc-root-cause-analyst (requested slot: sonnet;
# agentId a2ede104391abe269; provider model not reported by the Agent tool). Persisted verbatim by
# the orchestrator BEFORE calibration. self_reported_confidence is NOT used by any gate.
card_id: uc1-t1-pre-smoke-attempt-1-wave1c
mode: pre
author_role: sc:sc-root-cause-analyst
summary: >
  The plan maps all three spec requirements (R-001..R-003) to one task each
  (T-101..T-103), with no orphan tasks and no unmapped requirements. Coverage is
  complete only at the ID level. The tasks paraphrase the spec and drop the exact
  literal "Hello, Ada!" and the ValueError and exact-output assertions, so the
  plan has a specificity-loss risk on R-001 and R-003. This is a small,
  low-scope plan: 3 requirements, 3 tasks, one domain.
coverage:
  coverage_pct: 1.0
  coverage_pct_union: 1.0
  unmapped: []
  parsed_count: 3
  inferred_count: 0
  # S_scope=3, S_domains=1 (code+tests; treated as single-domain for this fixture), S_dev_density=0.0
findings:
  - id: F-001
    title: R-001 exact greeting literal not carried into T-101
    severity: medium
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: specificity-loss risk
    claim: >
      spec.md:6 requires the exact string "Hello, Ada!" for input Ada.
      proposed.md:4 says only "returning the required greeting", with no literal
      and no example input. An implementer could pick a different format (for
      example "Hello, Ada" without the "!") and still satisfy the task text.
    citations: ["spec.md:6", "proposed.md:4"]
    tag: grounded
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: >
      The task was written by reference to the requirement ID (the heading token
      "R-001" at proposed.md:3) rather than restating the acceptance literal.
      The mapping is by ID, so the content was never required to be copied. This
      cause is INFERRED, since the plan does not state its authoring method.
  - id: F-002
    title: R-003 test tasks do not state assertions, so exact-output check is unanchored
    severity: medium
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: specificity-loss risk
    claim: >
      spec.md:12 requires tests that exercise the ordinary greeting and the
      empty-input rejection. proposed.md:10 names both test categories but does
      not say the ordinary test asserts "Hello, Ada!" or that the empty-name test
      asserts ValueError. Together with F-001, the exact-output assertion
      appears nowhere in the tasklist. A test that calls greet("Ada") without
      checking the result would satisfy T-103 as worded.
    citations: ["spec.md:12", "proposed.md:10", "proposed.md:4"]
    tag: grounded
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: >
      Same ID-level authoring pattern as F-001. The spec's own wording at
      spec.md:12 ("exercise") is also weak, because it does not say "assert".
      The weakness is inherited upstream, so the plan cannot be fully blamed.
  - id: F-003
    title: Coverage 1.0 is ID-level only, not content-level
    severity: low
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: informational
    claim: >
      Each mapping rests on the "R-00N" token in the task heading
      (proposed.md:3, 6, 9) matching the spec heading (spec.md:5, 8, 11). The
      1.0 figure is therefore a lower bound on ID traceability, not on semantic
      fidelity. R-001 and R-003 are partial at content level (see F-001, F-002).
    citations: ["spec.md:5", "spec.md:8", "spec.md:11", "proposed.md:3", "proposed.md:6", "proposed.md:9"]
    tag: grounded
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: >
      The coverage metric (heading ID match) is coarser than the audit question
      (faithful coverage). A gap of this kind cannot lower coverage_pct, so it
      has to be reported as a finding.
  - id: F-004
    title: R-002 is faithfully carried
    severity: info
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: informational
    claim: >
      T-102 preserves ValueError and the empty-name condition. Whitespace-only
      names are unspecified in both documents, so this is a shared spec
      ambiguity and not a plan gap.
    citations: ["spec.md:9", "proposed.md:7"]
    tag: grounded
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: >
      Spec says "empty name"; neither document defines whether "   " counts as
      empty.
  - id: F-005
    title: Plan introduces signature greet(name) not named in spec
    severity: info
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: informational
    claim: >
      proposed.md:4 fixes the parameter shape greet(name). The spec names only
      "the greet function" (spec.md:6). This is a harmless plan-level
      specification, not an unauthorized expansion.
    citations: ["spec.md:6", "proposed.md:4"]
    tag: grounded
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: >
      The spec's "for Ada" and "empty name" language implies a single name
      parameter, so the plan's signature is a reasonable reading.
  - id: F-006
    title: Matrix span R-003 overruns the spec file length
    severity: info
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: informational
    claim: >
      The coverage matrix lists the R-003 span as "spec.md:11-13", but spec.md
      has 12 lines (line 12 is the last with content). The matrix cites a
      nonexistent line 13. The matrix row spec_ref ("spec.md:11-12") is correct,
      so there is no coverage impact. Any citation validator that checks span
      bounds could flag it.
    citations: ["spec.md:11", "spec.md:12"]
    tag: INFERRED
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: >
      The span was probably computed as "next heading line minus one" with an
      assumed trailing line. The 12-line count comes from the Read output; the
      cause of the overrun is inferred.
  - id: F-007
    title: Spec framing line (synthetic fixture) has no requirement
    severity: info
    deviation_class: n/a
    category: informational
    claim: >
      spec.md:1-3 is a title and a synthetic-fixture disclaimer with no MUST
      statement, so it correctly produces no requirement row. Every MUST
      (spec.md:6, 9, 12) falls inside a parsed span.
    citations: ["spec.md:1", "spec.md:3", "spec.md:6", "spec.md:9", "spec.md:12"]
    tag: grounded
    hypothesis_or_root_cause: n/a
risks:
  - >
    Silent acceptance of a wrong greeting format: a literal-free T-101 plus an
    assertion-free T-103 can pass review and tests while violating R-001
    (F-001, F-002). This is the primary load-bearing risk.
  - >
    False-positive green test run: tests that call greet without asserting the
    result or the raised exception would pass while not evidencing R-002/R-003
    (F-002, untested invariant).
  - >
    Edge-case drift on R-002: whitespace-only or None names are undefined, so
    different implementers could diverge. Blast radius is small (one function).
  - >
    Metric over-trust: a downstream gate reading coverage_pct=1.0 and
    S_dev_density=0.0 may treat the plan as fully faithful and skip content
    review (F-003).
  - >
    src/ and tests/ exist in the fixture. They were not read and are not
    treated as completed work. No claim here depends on them.
recommendations:
  - id: REC-1
    file: proposed.md
    change: >
      At proposed.md:4 (T-101), restate the literal: greet("Ada") returns exactly
      "Hello, Ada!".
    verifier: >
      Grep proposed.md for the literal "Hello, Ada!" inside the T-101 block; at
      least 1 match.
    priority: high
  - id: REC-2
    file: proposed.md
    change: >
      At proposed.md:10 (T-103), state the assertions: the ordinary test asserts
      the return value equals "Hello, Ada!", and the empty-name test asserts
      ValueError is raised, for example via pytest.raises(ValueError).
    verifier: >
      Grep the T-103 block for both "Hello, Ada!" and "ValueError"; both must be
      present.
    priority: high
  - id: REC-3
    file: spec.md
    change: >
      Optionally state whether whitespace-only names count as empty under R-002
      (spec.md:9), or record that they are out of scope.
    verifier: >
      The R-002 text contains an explicit whitespace statement, and T-102 at
      proposed.md:7 matches it.
    priority: low
  - id: REC-4

### C-1 (medium): R-001 exact literal not carried into T-101
- Spec: "The greet function MUST return the exact string Hello, Ada! for Ada." (spec.md:6)
- Task: "Implement greet(name) returning the required greeting." (proposed.md:4)

### C-2 (medium): R-003 tests do not state their assertions
- Spec: "Tests MUST exercise the ordinary greeting and empty-input rejection." (spec.md:12)
- Task: "Add ordinary and empty-name test cases." (proposed.md:10)

### C-3 (low/info): R-002 carried faithfully
- "MUST reject an empty name with ValueError" (spec.md:9) vs "Reject an empty name using ValueError." (proposed.md:7). Neither document defines whitespace-only names. This ambiguity is shared by both documents, not a plan gap.

### C-4 (info): plan adds signature greet(name)

- **Verifier:** The R-002 text carries the statement and T-102 (proposed.md:7) matches it.
- **Linked:** C-3
